body.en:
Kostolany wrote a number of books, and Korean readers know them largely through a boxed set issued as the Kostolany investment series. Editions and titles vary with the printing, so this article makes no claim about any individual volume's contents or publication details and treats only the themes that run through all of them.

What the books are actually about

Emphasis differs from book to book, but three subjects keep returning.

  • Cycles — markets rise and fall repeatedly, and the rising and falling has a recurring shape. The egg drawing and the six phases come from here.
  • Psychology — what moves prices is mostly how people react. The split between strong and weak hands belongs to this strand.
  • Patience — money and ideas are not enough without the capacity to sit through time. It appears on every list he gives of what successful speculation requires.

All three are about perspective rather than procedure. Nowhere is there a table of rules of the form “when this condition holds, do that”. Knowing this before starting removes most of the disappointment.

Reading a memoir carefully

These books are largely recollection, and recollection has its own grammar.

First, it is a survivor's memory. Contemporaries who approached the market the same way and disappeared did not write memoirs. Reasoning backwards from one book to a method cannot distinguish a trait that caused the success from a trait equally common among those who failed. That is a problem with the sample, not with the author's honesty.

Second, memory smooths as it becomes narrative. Decisions that rested on thin reasoning acquire reasons in the retelling — not through dishonesty, but because knowing the outcome reorganises the past around it. It is the same bias that leaves only the flattering parameter combination in mind after a backtest.

Third, the era differs. Information speed, transaction costs and market access are not what they were. Whether an observation that held then holds now is a separate question, and the book does not answer it for you.

Fourth, an anecdote is a sample of one. The more striking the episode, the longer it stays in memory, and the more often it feels like something that happens frequently. That a story is interesting and that the situation recurs are separate facts.

On editions and translations

One practical note. The same original has appeared under different titles at different times, and the editing and selection vary between printings. Choosing by title alone can mean buying substantially overlapping material twice, so check the table of contents first. It is also why this article names no specific edition — not writing down bibliographic details we have not verified is the same rule the rest of the site runs on.

Why they are still worth reading

The value is not predictive power but vocabulary: they teach a way of naming market states.

Names matter because a named state can be recorded, and a record can be scored. “I felt uneasy then” cannot be checked afterwards; “at the time I read it as close to a euphoric phase” can. Vocabulary converts an impression into a sentence capable of being wrong — and only what can be wrong can be learned from.

There is a second reason. These books treat markets as a problem of patience and temperament rather than one of forecasting accuracy. That focus differs sharply from most current discussion, and the difference itself repays attention. What this repository measured points the same way: nothing was gained on calling direction months ahead, while describing the present state left a quantity that can actually be scored.

What happens when you try to test the sentences

Take a hypothesis out of one of these books and try to verify it, and three walls arrive in order. Knowing about them in advance saves effort.

  • What counts as the right answer. You must decide which stretch of data “the euphoric phase” actually was — and that stretch is normally determined by looking backwards over data that has already happened. The reference label consults the future, so a real-time call is scored under conditions the label never faced.
  • The sample is smaller than it looks. Daily observations are plentiful; counted in cycles they run to a few dozen. That is not enough to rank methods that resemble one another.
  • Eras get mixed. A longer window adds sample and drags in periods with different costs and market structure. A shorter one reduces that problem and shrinks the sample further. Either way there is a price.

None of this is the books' fault. But it is worth knowing how much distance sits between “the book says so, therefore it holds” and “we measured it, and here is what came out”.

What to do once you have finished

The most useful thing to do after closing the book is to write your own rule down. Three lines is enough.

  • What state do you read the market as being in — write the name.
  • On what grounds — write observations that can be checked later.
  • What would you have to see to drop that reading — write it in advance.

The third line is the one that matters. Move the criterion after seeing the outcome and no judgement is ever wrong, and a judgement that cannot be wrong teaches nothing. It is the same reason this repository registers its thresholds before running an experiment and does not move them when the result disappoints.

Then come back to the note later. The thing to check is not whether the call was right but whether the grounds were genuinely observable. A correct call resting on unobservable grounds does not reproduce next time.

Once that habit sticks, the books change function. Sentences you underlined become items that can be checked, and as the checks accumulate you learn for yourself which of them hold in your own market. That is exactly the part no author can do for you.

title.ko: 코스톨라니와 워런 버핏은 무엇이 다른가 — 투기자와 투자자라는 두 어휘
title.en: Kostolany and Warren Buffett: two vocabularies, two different questions

description.ko: 코스톨라니와 워런 버핏(워렌 버핏)이 답하는 질문이 어떻게 다른지, 왜 우열 비교가 성립하기 어려운지, 그리고 채점 가능성이라는 기준을 정리한 교육용 해설.
description.en: How the questions Kostolany and Warren Buffett answer differ, why ranking them is the wrong frame, and what scoreability has to do with it. Educational only.

body.ko:
코스톨라니는 스스로를 투자자가 아니라 투기자라고 불렀다고 전해집니다. 워런 버핏(워렌 버핏)은 기업을 사서 오래 보유하는 쪽으로 널리 알려져 있고, 벤저민 그레이엄의 영향을 받아 사업의 가치를 따지는 방식으로 이야기됩니다. 둘을 나란히 놓고 누가 옳은지 겨루게 하는 글이 많지만, 실제로 두 사람은 서로 다른 질문에 답하고 있습니다.

질문이 다르다

버핏 계열의 질문은 「이 사업은 얼마짜리인가」입니다. 대상은 개별 기업이고, 판단의 재료는 수익성과 경쟁 구조이며, 시간 단위는 여러 해입니다. 시장 전체가 지금 어느 국면인지는 이 질문에서 부차적입니다.

코스톨라니 계열의 질문은 「지금 군중은 어디에 있는가」입니다. 대상은 시장 국면이고, 판단의 재료는 참여자의 태도와 거래의 열기이며, 시간 단위는 수개월에서 수년입니다. 개별 기업의 적정가치는 이 질문에서 부차적입니다.

두 질문 모두 정당하지만, 하나의 답이 다른 하나를 대신하지 못합니다. 좋은 기업을 골랐어도 시장 전체가 하락 레그면 몇 년간 불편할 수 있고, 국면을 잘 읽었어도 무엇을 들고 있느냐에 따라 결과가 갈립니다. 서로 다른 축의 답을 하나의 점수로 합칠 방법은 없습니다.

투자와 투기의 경계는 생각보다 흐리다

두 단어의 구분으로 널리 인용되는 것은 그레이엄이 남긴 정리입니다. 충분한 분석에 근거하고 원금의 안전과 적절한 수익을 기대할 수 있으면 투자이고, 그 조건을 만족하지 못하면 투기라는 취지로 알려져 있습니다.

깔끔한 정의처럼 보이지만 실제로 적용하면 경계가 흐려집니다. 「충분한 분석」이 어디까지인지, 「적절한 수익」이 얼마인지가 정해져 있지 않기 때문입니다. 같은 행동도 근거의 두께에 따라 이쪽이 되기도 하고 저쪽이 되기도 합니다.

그래서 실무적으로 더 쓸모 있는 구분은 명칭이 아니라 질문 쪽입니다. 내가 지금 무엇을 근거로 판단하고 있는가 — 사업의 형편인가, 참여자의 상태인가, 아니면 남들이 사고 있다는 사실인가. 세 번째라면 이름이 무엇이든 근거가 얇은 것입니다.

겹치는 지점

차이만 강조하면 오히려 부정확합니다. 두 사람의 이야기에는 겹치는 부분이 분명히 있습니다.

  • 군중을 따라가면 비싸게 산다. 표현은 달라도 두 사람 모두 같은 관찰을 반복합니다. 모두가 사고 싶어 할 때가 가장 비싼 때라는 것.
  • 인내가 비용을 줄인다. 자주 움직일수록 비용과 실수의 기회가 늘어난다는 점에 이견이 없습니다.
  • 모르는 것을 인정하는 편이 낫다. 자기 능력 범위 밖은 건드리지 않는다는 태도와, 시장은 예측 대상이 아니라 견디는 대상이라는 태도는 결이 비슷합니다.

흔한 오해 — 누가 더 부자인가로 비교하기

두 사람을 비교하는 글에서 가장 자주 등장하는 기준이 결과의 크기입니다. 그런데 개인의 결과는 표본 하나입니다. 표본 하나로는 방법의 우열을 가릴 수 없습니다.

게다가 우리가 이름을 아는 시장 인물은 거의 전부 살아남은 쪽입니다. 같은 방법을 쓰다 사라진 사람들의 결과는 어디에도 집계되지 않으므로, 유명한 사례를 모아 놓고 방법을 역산하면 언제나 그 방법이 좋아 보입니다. 이건 백테스트에서 상장폐지 종목을 빼는 것과 정확히 같은 오류입니다.

대결 구도가 자꾸 만들어지는 이유는 간단합니다. 읽히기 때문입니다. 다만 비교가 성립하려면 공통의 축이 있어야 하는데, 여기에는 그것이 없습니다. 같은 기간, 같은 자산, 같은 제약에서 두 방법을 나란히 돌려 본 기록이 없기 때문입니다.

시간 단위가 다르면 흔들림의 의미도 다르다

둘의 차이 가운데 실무적으로 가장 크게 갈리는 것이 변동을 무엇으로 보는가입니다. 판단의 시간 단위가 여러 해라면 중간의 흔들림은 대체로 견디면 지나가는 것에 가깝습니다. 시간 단위가 몇 달이라면 같은 흔들림이 판단의 성패 그 자체가 됩니다.

그래서 같은 하락을 놓고도 한쪽은 「예상 범위 안」이라고 말하고 다른 쪽은 「국면이 바뀌었다」고 말할 수 있습니다. 둘 다 자기 시간 단위에서는 일관된 진술입니다. 논쟁이 자주 헛도는 이유가 여기 있습니다 — 시간 단위를 밝히지 않은 채 결론만 주고받기 때문입니다.

덧붙여 — 대부분의 사람은 전업이 아니다

한 가지 더 짚어 둘 것이 있습니다. 두 사람 모두 시장을 본업으로 다뤘습니다. 쓸 수 있는 시간, 확인할 수 있는 자료, 감당할 수 있는 실패의 횟수가 대부분의 사람과 다릅니다.

방법을 고를 때 실제로 제약이 되는 것은 재능보다 이쪽인 경우가 많습니다. 하루에 몇 번 확인할 수 있는가, 틀렸을 때 다시 시도할 여유가 있는가. 유명한 사람의 방법을 그대로 옮겨 오기 전에 이 조건부터 맞춰 보는 편이 낫습니다.

이 사이트가 어느 쪽인가

어느 쪽도 아닙니다. Kostolany Watch는 종목을 고르지 않고, 언제 사고팔지도 말하지 않습니다. 하는 일은 하나입니다 — 지금 시장이 어떤 상태로 읽히는지 서술하고, 그 서술이 과거에 얼마나 맞았는지 함께 공개하는 것.

굳이 따지자면 다루는 질문은 코스톨라니 쪽에 가깝습니다. 이유는 그 질문이 더 훌륭해서가 아니라 채점하기 쉬워서입니다. 국면 판정은 매일 값이 나오고 나중에 맞았는지 틀렸는지 세어 볼 수 있습니다. 반면 「이 사업은 얼마짜리인가」에 대한 답은 회수까지 몇 년이 걸리고, 그동안 쌓이는 표본이 너무 적어 방법의 우열을 통계적으로 가리기 어렵습니다.

채점 가능성을 기준으로 삼는 것은 겸손이 아니라 실용입니다. 채점할 수 없는 주장은 틀려도 틀린 줄 모르고, 틀린 줄 모르면 고칠 수도 없습니다.

다만 이 선택에도 대가가 있습니다. 국면 판정에 쓰는 정답 라벨은 지나간 데이터를 뒤에서 되돌아보며 붙인 것이라, 그 라벨 자체가 미래를 참조합니다. 그래서 실시간 판정은 라벨이 상정한 만큼 깔끔할 수 없고, 정확한 칸을 집는 데는 구조적인 상한이 생깁니다. 이 사이트가 방향과 정확한 칸을 따로 표시하는 이유입니다.

두 어휘를 함께 쓰려면

둘을 섞어 쓰고 싶다면, 각 어휘가 어떤 질문에 답하는지 표시해 두는 것이 안전합니다. 국면 판단은 무엇을 들고 있을지를 정해 주지 않고, 가치 판단은 지금이 어떤 국면인지를 말해 주지 않습니다. 두 답을 한 문장에 섞으면 나중에 어느 쪽이 틀렸는지 짚을 수 없게 됩니다.

구분해 두는 습관 하나면 충분합니다. 판단을 적을 때 어느 질문에 답한 것인지 함께 적어 두는 것. 그것만으로도 나중에 복기가 가능해집니다.

body.en:
Kostolany is said to have called himself not an investor but a speculator. Warren Buffett is known for buying businesses and holding them for a long time, and is usually discussed in terms of appraising a business, in the tradition of Benjamin Graham. Plenty of writing sets the two against each other to decide who was right. In fact they are answering different questions.

Different questions

The Buffett-side question is “what is this business worth?” The object is an individual company, the material is profitability and competitive position, and the clock runs in years. Which phase the whole market is in is secondary to that question.

The Kostolany-side question is “where is the crowd right now?” The object is the market's phase, the material is participant behaviour and the heat of trading, and the clock runs from months to years. The fair value of any single company is secondary to that one.

Both questions are legitimate, and neither answer substitutes for the other. Owning a good business through a down leg can be uncomfortable for years, and reading the phase well still leaves the result dependent on what you happen to hold. There is no way to combine answers on different axes into one score.

The line between investment and speculation is blurrier than it looks

The distinction most often quoted comes from Graham: an operation resting on thorough analysis, promising safety of principal and an adequate return, is investment; anything failing those conditions is speculation.

It reads as a clean definition and blurs on contact. How thorough is thorough, and how much is adequate, are not specified. The same action lands on either side depending on how thick the reasoning underneath it was.

So the more useful distinction in practice is not the label but the question: what am I actually reasoning from? The condition of a business, the state of the participants, or the fact that other people are buying. If it is the third, the grounds are thin whatever you call it.

Where they overlap

Emphasising only the differences would be inaccurate. Several observations recur in both.

  • Following the crowd means paying more. The wording differs; the observation that the most eager moment is the most expensive one does not.
  • Patience lowers cost. Neither disputes that moving often accumulates expense and multiplies the chances of error.
  • Admitting what you do not know pays. Staying inside a circle of competence and treating the market as something to sit through rather than forecast are close relatives.

The common misframe — comparing net worth

The criterion that shows up most often in these comparisons is the size of the outcome. But one person's outcome is a single sample, and a single sample cannot rank methods.

Worse, almost every market figure whose name we know is a survivor. Those who used the same approach and vanished are counted nowhere, so reasoning backwards from famous cases always flatters the method. It is the same error as dropping delisted names from a backtest.

The reason the head-to-head keeps getting written is simple: it gets read. But a comparison needs a shared axis, and there is none here — no record of the two approaches run side by side over the same period, the same assets and the same constraints.

Different clocks make volatility mean different things

The difference that matters most in practice is what a swing counts as. If the judgement runs over years, an interim drawdown is largely something to sit through. If it runs over months, the same drawdown is the success or failure of the judgement itself.

So the same decline lets one side say “within expectations” and the other say “the phase has changed”, and both are consistent inside their own clock. This is why the argument so often spins: conclusions get exchanged without the time horizon attached to them.

One more thing — most people are not doing this full time

Both men worked the market as their occupation. The hours available, the material they could check, the number of failures they could absorb — none of it matches the situation of most readers.

When choosing a method, that constraint binds more often than talent does. How many times a day can you look? Is there room to try again after being wrong? Matching those conditions comes before importing anyone's approach wholesale.

Which side is this site on

Neither. Kostolany Watch does not pick securities and does not say when to buy or sell. It does one thing: describe the state the market currently reads as being in, and publish how often that description was right historically.

If forced to choose, the question it works on is closer to Kostolany's — not because that question is better, but because it is easier to score. A regime call produces a value every day and can be counted right or wrong afterwards. An answer to “what is this business worth?” takes years to resolve, and accumulates far too few observations along the way to separate methods statistically.

Choosing on scoreability is pragmatism rather than modesty. A claim that cannot be scored does not announce itself when it is wrong, and what does not announce itself cannot be corrected.

The choice has a cost of its own, though. The reference labels used to score regime calls are assigned by looking back over data that has already happened, so the labels themselves consult the future. A real-time call can therefore never be as tidy as the label assumes, and pinning the exact box acquires a structural ceiling. That is why direction and the exact box are reported separately here.

Using both vocabularies

If you want both, label which question each is answering. A phase reading does not tell you what to hold, and a valuation does not tell you which phase this is. Blend the two answers into one sentence and you lose the ability to say later which half was wrong.

One habit is enough: when writing down a judgement, write down which question it answered. That alone makes a review possible afterwards.
